text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000018's 99215 rate stays well above expected even after risk adjustment, but the few charts returned support the billed levels, so the pattern is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The panel is genuinely complex: most 99215s fall on patients with 5+ conditions, and few are on low-complexity patients. Yet the 99215 share runs roughly two to five times the all-provider share in every complexity band, including patients with 0 conditions, so panel acuity alone does not explain the excess. The documentation points the other way: none of the 9 documented 99215 claims was below the billed level, and only 2 of 23 notes had moderate-plus data reviewed without a lab line, which is a weak signal of inflated notes. Nine charts is too few to outweigh a strong risk-adjusted excess, and the notes could still match the billing without matching the visit. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215s, such as C0012483 and C0012524 (same patient, no chronic conditions, back pain and urinary diagnoses) and C0012538 (Z09 follow-up only), then widen the records sample for 99215s in the 3–5+ condition bands to see whether the high MDM documentation holds up."}
